title: Working with Jack Lane and brass bands versus orchestras for dances
summary: Lane passed on dance jobs, Brown played tuba with him, and orchestras suited dancers better than brass bands.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: You say Papa Lane would turn some of his dance jobs over to you then, when he'd got them?
Oh, yes. A great many times he'd have bands, he'd dance us downtown, and he'd give us a job. Did you ever work? And of course, he'd get his booking fees. Yeah.
Did you ever work in any band with Jack Lane? Jack Lane? Jack Lane?
Yes, I played tuba with Jack Lane, Jack Lane quite a number of times, across the river, as I remember, different affairs.
Would that be dancers or...? Dances, yeah, dancers. What sort of a rhythm did he get?

See, we used to employ brass bands for dances too, great big dances. Now, they used to have dances out in all the bands, all the large pavilions that have a very big brass band in order to be heard. Well, that was the habit. But later on, like in Mellenburg and in West End, they had certain pavilions out there, but it all depended upon the chairman of the committee. If he wanted an orchestra, he'd specify an orchestra, you know. Or if he wanted to hire a brass band, he'd hire a brass band. But as a general rule, the orchestra used to sound better to the dancers in the brass band. In fact, they could dance much better than they could to the brass band. The brass band couldn't get into the groove like the orchestra would come.
Do you remember who was in the Papa Lane's band? Any of the other musicians that you can think of now? Papa Lane's band?
I remember a lot of them, but the names I can't. You'd have to get that for Jack Lane himself. I imagine he remembers all the names of them.
